newsitem.title: USA: Zurich to give $13mln to Bridgeport, Conn.
newsitem.headline: Zurich to give $13mln to Bridgeport, Conn.

text.p: Zurich Reinsurance Centre Holdings will contribute $12.5 million to economic development programs in Bridgeport, Conn., a spokeswoman for Gov. John Rowland (R) said on Wednesday.

The contribution was agreed to after some Connecticut lawmakers had criticized a state law which awarded $190 million in tax breaks to Zurich for its planned relocation to Stamford, Conn., from New York.
Rowland is supporting efforts to change the 1994 law, though it would not be retroactive, Rowland spokeswoman Nuala Forde told Reuters.
Senate Majority Leader George Jepsen (D) has argued that nearby Bridgeport, the state's largest city, with a population of 138,000, was more badly in need of jobs than Stamford.
About $10 million of the Zurich funds will go towards a new baseball stadium in Bridgeport, Forde said. Another $2.5 million will be for a sports museum.
"This is certainly a shot in the arm for Bridgeport, which everyone agress needs the investment quickly," Forde said.
She said Rowland has earmarked $125 million for economic development in Bridgeport over the next five years.
"This is simply part of our effort to be a good corporate citizen," Zurich spokesman Nick Carter told Reuters.
"The relocation to Stamford would affect approximately 300 people now working at Zurich Centre Group and Zurich Reinsurance in New York," he said.
The 300 employees would join 80 Zurich Reinsurance employees already working in Stamford, he said.

"As these businesses are continuing to grow, it is expected that by the year 2000, when the relocation is currently expected to be finished, the total number of employees relocating to Stamford will be 400," Carter said.
